# cleura_openstack_volume_recovery_service (Resource)

Switches on Cleura's **Recovery service** (disaster recovery) for a **block volume**.
The volume itself is usually managed by the OpenStack provider's [`openstack_blockstorage_volume_v3`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/terraform-provider-openstack/openstack/latest/docs/resources/blockstorage_volume_v3).
This resource adds the Recovery service to it by ID, so the two providers work side by side.

- `retention_days` and `immutable` are changed in place, without switching the service off.
- If the service is already on for the volume, creating this resource takes it over and applies the configured settings.
  `immutable` defaults to `false`, so to keep an immutable service immutable, set `immutable = true`, or import the resource first so the plan shows its current settings.
- Destroying the resource, or removing it from your configuration, switches the service off.
  Terraform waits until Cleura has finished stopping it, usually 10 to 20 seconds, so a `terraform destroy` that also deletes the volume works in one run.
  With immutable recovery points, Terraform doesn't wait: see below.

Cleura takes a recovery point of the volume once a day and keeps each one for `retention_days`.
See Cleura's [Recovery service](https://docs.cleura.cloud/kna1/background/recovery-service/) documentation.

~> **Switching the service off deletes the volume's recovery points**, unless they are immutable, and this can't be undone.
That happens when you destroy this resource, remove it from your configuration, or rename it without a `moved` block.
For volumes whose recovery points you can't afford to lose, add `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`.
It blocks destroying or replacing the resource, but not deleting its block from the configuration, because the setting goes with the block.
To stop managing the service with Terraform but keep it on, replace the resource block with a `removed` block with `lifecycle { destroy = false }` (Terraform 1.7 or later), or use `terraform state rm`.

~> **Immutable recovery points** (`immutable = true`) can't be deleted, by hand or by switching the service off, until their retention has passed.
You can still change or switch off the service at any time; switching it off stops new recovery points.
The volume can't be deleted until the last recovery point has expired, up to `retention_days` later, so Terraform doesn't wait for it and warns instead.

### Moving from other tooling

If other tooling switched the service on, create this resource for the volume, or import it.
Then remove the other tooling's state **without** destroying it, because destroying it would switch the service off.
In Terraform, use a `removed` block with `lifecycle { destroy = false }`, or `terraform state rm`.

### Prerequisites

The provider must be authenticated and have a `region`.
The volume's project defaults to the provider's `project_id`; set `project_id`, and `region` if needed, on the resource when the volume lives elsewhere.
See the provider's [Authentication](../index.md#authentication) documentation.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    cleura = {
      source = "cleura/cleura"
    }
    openstack = {
      source = "terraform-provider-openstack/openstack"
    }
  }
}

# The volume, managed by the OpenStack provider. Its volume type must support
# the Recovery service.
resource "openstack_blockstorage_volume_v3" "data" {
  name        = "data"
  size        = 100
  volume_type = "cbs"
}

# Switch on the Recovery service for the volume and keep recovery points for
# 10 days (10 or 30).
resource "cleura_openstack_volume_recovery_service" "data" {
  volume_id      = openstack_blockstorage_volume_v3.data.id
  retention_days = 10
}
```

To protect several volumes created with `for_each`, use `for_each` here too:

```terraform
resource "cleura_openstack_volume_recovery_service" "disks" {
  for_each = openstack_blockstorage_volume_v3.disks

  volume_id      = each.value.id
  retention_days = 30
}
```

## Import

```shell
# A Recovery service is imported by its volume's ID. Region and project default
# to the provider's; prefix them as <project_id>/<volume_id> or
# <region>/<project_id>/<volume_id> to name them explicitly.
terraform import cleura_openstack_volume_recovery_service.data 5c9a1f0e-2b3d-4e5f-8a6b-7c8d9e0f1a2b
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `retention_days` (Number) How many days recovery points are kept: `10` or `30`. Changed in place.
- `volume_id` (String) ID of the volume, for example `openstack_blockstorage_volume_v3.data.id`. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `immutable` (Boolean) Whether recovery points are immutable: kept for their full retention, even after the service is switched off, and the volume can't be deleted until then. Defaults to `false`. Changed in place.
- `project_id` (String) OpenStack project of the volume. Defaults to the provider's `project_id`. Changing it forces a new resource.
- `region` (String) Region of the volume. Defaults to the provider's `region`. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The volume's ID.
- `started_at` (String) When the Recovery service was switched on (RFC 3339).
